notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish or beer — a label alone doesn’t qualify. The Liège canon: boulets à la liégeoise (sauce lapin with sirop de Liège), the pearl-sugar gaufre de Liège, salade liégeoise, péket, sirop de Liège and Herve cheese. Beer & breweries are their own grouped layer (Val-Dieu, Brasserie C, Jupiler’s Jupille). A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

notes.title: Web-searched in French and fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, Gault&Millau, Le Soir, La Libre, RTBF, La Meuse, L’Avenir, Visit Liège, Wallonie Belgique Tourisme, beer authorities and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor/RateBeer never count toward the two-source bar.

places.w: The early-17th-c. red-brick mansion of the arms merchant Jean Curtius on the Meuse, reopened in 2009 as one museum merging archaeology, weaponry, glass, decorative arts and Mosan religious art over 5,000 m².
The 16th-c. palace of the Prince-Bishops who ruled Liège for eight centuries, dominating Place Saint-Lambert; today the Palais de Justice, its arcaded first courtyard is open to walk through.
Romanesque collegiate church with a twin-towered westwork, home to Renier de Huy's baptismal font (c. 1107–1118) — a lost-wax brass basin on ten oxen, a masterpiece of Mosan art.

The 374-step stairway (1881) cut straight up the hillside from Hors-Château to the Citadelle, built so soldiers could reach town without the alleys — Liège's emblem and its best free climb, with a panorama over the roofs and the Meuse.
Santiago Calatrava's white steel-and-glass vault (2009) — a station with no façade, just a 160 m canopy over the tracks; worth the detour even if you arrive by car.

places.ad: Parc de la Boverie 3, 4020 Liège, Belgium
places.w: The city's fine-arts museum in a 1905 Exhibition palace on the Boverie island park, with a glass extension for blockbuster shows run in partnership with the Louvre; Ingres, Monet, Picasso and the Walloon school.

places.ad: Place de la Cathédrale, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Gothic cathedral since 1802 (after the revolutionaries razed Saint-Lambert); its Trésor holds the reliquary bust of Saint Lambert and the gold reliquary Charles the Bold gave in penance for sacking the city.

The 1930s Sauvenière swimming baths, an Art Deco modernist landmark, reborn as a civic culture centre with exhibitions on memory and citizenship (incl. the permanent 'Plus jamais ça!' Holocaust route).
The Province's folk-life museum in the 17th-c. Friars Minor convent — a century of Walloon everyday life, crafts, dialect and the Liège puppets (with marionnette shows).

One of the four UNESCO 'Major Mining Sites of Wallonia' and one of only a handful of European coal mines you can still descend — ex-miners guide you 30 and 60 m down the shafts of the Trembleur colliery (closed 1980).
The Dutch-built (1818–23) citadel crowning the rock above the Meuse at Huy — a Nazi prison and Gestapo jail in WWII, now a memorial museum with sweeping river views.
Gothic collegiate church on the Meuse with the great rose window 'Li Rondia' and a treasury holding Mosan reliquary shrines of the 12th–13th c.

Victor Besme's 1880 octagonal pavilion over Spa's most famous iron-rich spring, named for Peter the Great who took the cure here in 1717 — taste the water, see the Livre d'Or painting of famous curistes.
The 7 km Ardennes circuit of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1921 and its legendary Eau Rouge–Raidillon climb; tours, a museum in Stavelot abbey and race weekends all season.

Under Place Saint-Lambert: the excavated foundations of the vanished Cathedral of Saint-Lambert (razed 1794), a Gallo-Roman villa and finds back to the Mesolithic — the city's birthplace, walked underground.
Former Benedictine abbey church with a flamboyant-Gothic nave under a dazzling painted star vault, a Romanesque westwork and a Renaissance portal — Liège's most beautiful interior.
Museum of the 'Free Republic of Outremeuse' devoted to Tchantchès, Liège's cheeky wooden-puppet hero — his costumes, the Bisscheroux marionettes and puppet shows in season.
The 1820 neoclassical Théâtre royal, Wallonia's opera house, with a modern rooftop extension; Grétry's heart is in an urn at the foot of his statue outside.

places.ad: Quai Édouard Van Beneden 22, 4020 Liège, Belgium
places.w: The University of Liège's aquarium (2,500 fish in some 50 tanks) and zoological museum in the 19th-c. Institut de Zoologie on the Meuse — a whale skeleton, dioramas and a cabinet of curiosities.
One of Liège's seven collegiate churches (founded c. 987) with a fortress-like Romanesque tower; inside, a carved Brabant altarpiece of the Passion of St Denis (early 16th c.).

places.ad: Coteaux de la Citadelle, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: 86 ha of terraced hillside orchards, vineyards, stairways and alleys between Hors-Château and the Citadelle — Liège's green lung, laureate of the Council of Europe Landscape Award; walk the Terrasses des Minimes for the views.
The old market square in front of the 18th-c. town hall 'La Violette', ringed by café terraces; the Perron fountain at its centre is the symbol of Liège's civic liberties since the Middle Ages.
An 18th-c. merchant-banker's mansion on Féronstrée kept as a period house museum — Liège furniture, Cordoba leather wall-hangings, tapestries and stucco ceilings of the prince-bishops' golden age.

places.n: Maison de la Métallurgie et de l'Industrie de Liège
places.w: Industrial-heritage museum in the old Espérance-Longdoz steelworks — a working 17th-c.-style forge, blast-furnace models and the story of the coal and steel that made Liège.

places.n: Musée des Transports en commun de Wallonie
places.w: Old Vennes tram depot full of Liège trams, trolleybuses and buses from horse-drawn days on — a nostalgic stop now the city's new tram is running again.

The Interallied Memorial on the Cointe hill: a 75 m tower and a basilica raised in the 1930s by the WWI Allies to honour the 1914 defence of Liège — the lift up the tower gives the city's best panorama.
Show cave on the Amblève at Aywaille — a walk through vast chambers ending in what the caves bill as one of the longest underground boat rides in Europe.
Belgium's best-known waterfall on the Amblève near Stavelot, with a chairlift up to the Montagne de Lancre viewpoint above.
Ruined medieval fortress on a rock above Theux, seat of the old marquisate of Franchimont; its towers and casemates can be explored.
Belgium's highest point (694 m) on the Hautes Fagnes plateau — the gateway to the raised-bog boardwalks of the High Fens nature reserve.
The former Cistercian abbey on the Meuse at Seraing where Val-Saint-Lambert has blown lead crystal since 1826 — the Cristal Discovery visit shows glassblowers at work and two centuries of pieces.

places.ad: Quai de la Batte, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Every Sunday morning since 1561: Belgium's oldest and biggest street market stretches 2 km along the Meuse quays — fruit, Herve cheese, live poultry, flowers, books, and péket and gaufres to keep you going.

places.ad: Colline d'Annette et Lubin, Spa, Belgium
places.w: The modern glass thermal baths on Annette-et-Lubin hill, reached by funicular from the town centre — naturally carbonated Spa waters in the town that gave every 'spa' its name, a UNESCO Great Spa Town of Europe since 2021.

places.n: Musée de la Ville d'eaux (Villa Royale)
places.w: In Queen Marie-Henriette's Villa Royale: the story of Spa as Europe's 'Café of Europe' resort, with the painted-wood 'Jolités de Spa' souvenirs; the Spa horse museum is in the stables.

The former prince-abbey of Stavelot-Malmedy, its 11th-c. church foundations laid open, now three museums: the Principality's history, Guillaume Apollinaire, and the Spa-Francorchamps circuit museum of F1 cars and bikes.

10th-c. collegiate church rebuilt in Gothic style (1506–42) on the aristocratic Mont-Saint-Martin — where the feast of Corpus Christi (Fête-Dieu) was first celebrated in 1246; 16th-c. stained glass and calvary.
Notger's collegiate church of 979 with a rare Romanesque west choir — currently closed for a long restoration, but the building site opens for themed guided visits.
In the heart of Parc d'Avroy, a museum of ~3,000 works of 'situated art' made in workshops by artists with mental disabilities — one of the most original collections in Belgium.
The Outremeuse birthplace of composer André-Modeste Grétry (1741), with his instruments, scores and period furnishings.

places.n: Hôtel de Ville de Liège (La Violette)
places.w: The 1714–18 town hall known as 'La Violette', its Louis XIV façade on the Place du Marché hiding a sumptuous interior of marble, stucco and grisailles.

The most famous of Brialmont's ring of forts: on 15 Aug 1914 a German 'Big Bertha' shell blew up its magazine and entombed 350 defenders — the crater, the crypt-necropolis and a scenographic museum relive the moment.
A fairytale 16th-c. moated castle with a chequerboard sandstone-and-limestone façade, owned by the Province; the interior is closed for long-term restoration but the gardens and park are open.

places.ad: Barrage de la Gileppe, Jalhay, Belgium
places.w: One of Europe's oldest dams (inaugurated 1878), crowned by the 13.5 m sandstone Lion of the Gileppe; free access to the crest, the panoramic tower and lakeside walks.
A 1354 castle on a rock spur above the Warche gorge, rebuilt in 1969 as the archetypal fortress — 75-minute guided tours of armour, tapestries and furniture, plus the Reinhardstein waterfall walk.
Spa's 19th-c. reservoir lake in the woods just north of town — pedal boats, fishing and an easy lakeside loop.
The restored former monastery of Malmedy, now the town's heritage and visitor centre.

places.ad: Rue de la Grotte 128, 4400 Flémalle, Belgium
places.w: A 30-ha prehistory park around the Ramioul cave above the Meuse — hands-on flint-knapping, fire-making, reconstructed camps and a hunting trail; plan half a day.

places.ad: Rue du Château d'Aigremont 1, 4400 Flémalle, Belgium
places.w: Early-18th-c. Liège château high above the Meuse at Les Awirs, classified exceptional heritage — guided visits of its panelled rooms, a staircase of restored trompe-l'œil paintings and French gardens.

places.n: Centre Touristique de la Laine et de la Mode
places.ad: Rue de la Chapelle 30, 4800 Verviers, Belgium
places.w: In a former Verviers textile mill, the story of the wool town that dressed Europe — from fleece to yarn, historic Verviers-built machines and the wool merchants' office.

Huy's lively main square in front of the town hall, centred on Li Bassinia, the bronze fountain whose oldest parts date from 1406 — one of the 'four wonders' of Huy with the Rondia rose window, the bridge and the castle.
The Province's 22-ha leisure park around the moated Wégimont castle on the Herve plateau — open-air pools, boating, minigolf and picnic lawns; a favourite family day out from Liège.
Five-hectare landscape park in the city centre with a pond, statues and remarkable trees (a Cedar of Lebanon, bald cypresses, plane-tree alleys); the Trinkhall Museum sits in it.
The University's former botanical garden (c. 3 ha), now a city park with some 400 trees including fifteen Belgian 'champion' specimens — sequoias, ginkgo, Japanese zelkova — and 19th-c. glasshouses.

Liège's famous pedestrian nightlife block between the Boulevard de la Sauvenière and Pont d'Avroy — some thirty bars in four little streets, packed with students and the whole city at weekends, with no fixed closing time.
Outremeuse's narrow restaurant lane — one cooking smell after another, small cafés and terraces, the nerve centre of the quarter's nightlife a step from the Meuse.

Founded c. 980 by Notger, Liège's first prince-bishop, who is buried here; an 11th-c. west tower fronts the 18th-c. rotunda church, and the cloister walls are lined with canons' tombstones — freshly restored.

places.ad: Passerelle La Belle Liégeoise, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: The 294 m footbridge (2016) linking Guillemins station to the Boverie park across the Meuse, named after the revolutionary feminist Théroigne de Méricourt.
Historic concert and comedy hall on Pont d'Avroy, one of Liège's main live-music venues.

Liège's main playhouse in the neoclassical Société libre d'Émulation building (Julien Koenig, 1934–39; the 1779 society's first hall was burned in the 1914 reprisals) — classified 1998, rebuilt by Pierre Hebbelinck & Pierre de Wit and reopened Oct 2013 with a 557-seat hall, bar and the Baci restaurant.
One of Liège's oldest cafés and the locals' answer to 'where for boulets?' — boulet-frites in sauce lapin is the house institution; a past Diamond Boulet winner of the Gay Boulet brotherhood.
Artisan waffle shop in the Mineurs quarter since 2010, making traditional pearl-sugar Liège waffles with good butter and eggs; also a house range of ice creams.
One Michelin star — the province's flagship table, a family hotel-restaurant by the Spa-Francorchamps circuit; chef Mathieu Vande Velde's produce-and-terroir menus.
One Michelin star on the Ourthe quay at Comblain-au-Pont — creative, flavour-forward cooking in a small riverside house.
One Michelin star plus a Green Star — Arabelle Meirlaen's intensely vegetal 'intuitive cuisine' built on her potager in the Condroz; Gault&Millau prize-winner 2025.
One Michelin star in a converted Condroz farmhouse at Soheit-Tinlot — refined, seasonal country cooking.
One Michelin star since 2024 for chef Marie Trignon's table in Modave, in the Liège Condroz.

places.ad: Chaussée de la Seigneurie 13, 4800 Petit-Rechain (Verviers), Belgium
places.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand at Petit-Rechain (Verviers) — a keen-priced seasonal menu.
Michelin Bib Gourmand in Verviers, the old wool town on the Vesdre.
Michelin Bib Gourmand in Verviers.
Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2025 — Thai cooking in the Condroz village of Ouffet.
The only abbey brewery still brewing inside its abbey walls in Wallonia's Pays de Herve — Val-Dieu ales poured in the abbey tavern; Saturday guided abbey + brewery tours with beer and Herve cheese.
Family brewery at the Three Borders in Hombourg — Joup, Brice and the Aubel triple; pub with food Wed–Sun, cheese shop, and Saturday tours.
Gault&Millau-listed (13.5/20, Nov 2023) gastronomic table in the little Château Peltzer, Verviers — CLOSED August 2024 (Paris Match).
Gault&Millau-listed creative bistronomy in Verviers.
Gault&Millau-listed restaurant on Place Albert Ier in Verviers.
Gault&Millau-listed restaurant on Verviers' Place du Marché.
Gault&Millau-listed modern French restaurant on the Barisart road out of Spa (Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024).
Gault&Millau-listed table in Herve, capital of the cheese country.
Gault&Millau-listed — worldly cooking built on local products, in Seraing.
Gault&Millau-listed: in an elegant natural-stone building, chefs Sami Chebil and Deniz Bâg mix tradition and modernity with precise, balanced plates.
Gault&Millau-listed family restaurant in Theux, warm welcome and accessible cooking.
Gault&Millau-listed restaurant near the basilica of Chèvremont in Chaudfontaine.
Gault&Millau-listed cocktail bar-restaurant in Herstal — bold creations and tapas.
Gault&Millau-listed: chef Mirko Radermeker's inventive cooking of local products with international accents, in Eupen.
Gault&Millau-listed fusion kitchen in Eupen — French classics lightened with Asian notes.

places.ad: Place du Vieux Tilleul 14 (Fontin), 4130 Esneux, Belgium
places.w: Gault&Millau-listed: a renovated farmhouse in the Ourthe valley cooking local artisans' produce over a wood fire.
Gault&Millau-listed: Narbonne-born chef Manuel Béjar brings the French south to Tilff on the Ourthe.
Gault&Millau-listed warm restaurant in Tilff.
Gault&Millau-listed elegant Italian restaurant on Aywaille's square.
Gault&Millau-listed: Grégory Baruthio Muller's seasonal French cooking with a southern lilt, in Huy.
Gault&Millau-listed — an original Italian-meets-Vietnamese kitchen in Huy.
Gault&Millau-listed (and Michelin Bib Gourmand) Italian with Sicilian accents and an open kitchen, in Wanze.

places.ad: Rue Naxhelet 1 (Domaine de Naxhelet), 4520 Wanze, Belgium
places.w: Gault&Millau-listed table of the Naxhelet estate — chef François Durand cooks from the estate's own vegetable garden.
Gault&Millau-listed countryside bistro with a mountain-chalet feel in Waimes, near the Hautes Fagnes.

places.ad: Rue de la Gare 23 (Hôtel Ravel), 4950 Waimes, Belgium
places.w: Gault&Millau-listed intimate restaurant in the Hôtel Ravel — reservation only.
Gault&Millau-listed: chef David Simons cooks local produce and garden vegetables in Waimes.

places.ad: Esplanade de la Grâce 1, 4800 Verviers, Belgium
places.w: Jean-Philippe Darcis — 'ambassador of Belgian chocolate' and pioneer of the macaron in Belgium — runs his shop, tasting room, workshop and a walk-through chocolate museum near the centre of Verviers.

places.ad: Boulevard de la Sauvenière 70, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: One Michelin star — creative South-American-inspired cooking on the Sauvenière, one of the city's two starred tables in the 2026 guide.

One Michelin star — a 'brasserie gastronomique' set, per Michelin, in a pretty little castle some 10 km outside the centre (address Allée des Érables), all old beams and a summer terrace; creative French cooking.

places.ad: Rue de la Goffe 8, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand bistro behind the Goffe market hall — a lyonnais-style room serving generous Liège and French bistro classics.

places.ad: Boulevard Émile de Laveleye 191, 4020 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand in Longdoz — a good-value, market-driven bistro menu across the river from the centre.
Michelin Bib Gourmand on Féronstrée, the museum street — a short seasonal set menu at a keen price.

places.ad: Rue de la Cathédrale 25, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2025 — farm-to-table, creative French cooking in the Carré near the cathedral.
Michelin-selected contemporary French table run by sommelier Élodie Timmermans — the wine list is the point.
The Carré's mythic, wildly decorated bar — #8 in The European Bar Guide's Top 100 of 2025; big beer list, often-free gigs, open till 4am.
Liège's own city microbrewery since 2012, tucked at the foot of the Montagne de Bueren — brews Curtius (the city's blonde), Black {C} and Smash {C}; tours and tasting workshops, taproom Thu–Sun.

The péket temple in restored 18th-c. houses off Place du Marché — dozens of flavoured jenevers by the glass, and in its Amon Nanesse restaurant Liège dishes cooked with péket; the boulets here were filmed for Darley Newman's PBS travel series.
Outremeuse taverne named for the city's puppet hero and his wife — terroir cooking, boulets in sauce lapin and the folklore of the 'free republic' quarter.
Old-world tavern a few steps from the cathedral, ranked #76 in The European Bar Guide's Top 100 European bars — a charming room from another era.
The busiest of the Place du Marché café-restaurants (the name is Walloon for 'the birds') — generous Walloon specialities like rabbit stewed in beer and big boulets on a terrace facing the Perron.
Old-school brasserie looking onto the Opéra royal; its boulets won the Confrérie du Gay Boulet's Diamond Boulet in 2008.

places.ad: Rue des Anciennes Houblonnières 2, 4020 Jupille (Liège), Belgium
places.w: Birthplace of Jupiler, Belgium's best-selling pils — AB InBev's giant Meuse-side brewery in Jupille, visitable by reservation (breweryvisits.com).

places.ad: Rue de la Casquette 5, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand Italian enoteca on Rue de la Casquette in the centre; also a Culture Trip lunch pick.
Michelin Bib Gourmand trattoria in Grivegnée, east Liège.
Michelin-selected restaurant on the Esplanade Albert Ier.
Michelin-selected and Gault&Millau-listed: Sébastien Lambert-Carabin's contemporary cooking of local produce in a monumentally renovated 17th-c. building on En Neuvice, near the Batte.
Michelin-selected Italian restaurant on Rue Grétry, across the river from the centre.
Gault&Millau-listed modern brasserie facing the Guillemins station — consistently high quality across a wide menu.
Gault&Millau-listed neo-gastronomic table on Rue des Carmes — bold, precise cooking that follows the seasons.
Gault&Millau-listed French restaurant on Rue des Clarisses near the Carré.
Gault&Millau-listed: chef Vincenzo Calderone goes back to his Puglian and Sicilian roots with honest, full-flavoured cooking in the reconverted Val-Benoît.

places.ad: Place du Vingt Août 16, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Gault&Millau-listed restaurant inside the Théâtre de Liège — lively contemporary Mediterranean cooking that follows the seasons.

Gault&Millau-listed, accessible restaurant where the main product takes centre stage, often cooked over the barbecue. Revived by Yann Stroobant (ex-Cabale) at the 1987 Hors-Château address (Le Fooding).
Gault&Millau-listed bistro-brasserie on Rue des Guillemins, one of Moustique's 12 Liège addresses for boulets and regional dishes.
Gault&Millau-listed restaurant at Rue des Mineurs 6 that introduced Georgian cuisine to Liège (Moustique).
Gault&Millau-listed wine and cocktail bar on Rue Bonne Fortune, also promoted by the city's tourist office.
Gault&Millau's 2026 Walloon H!P (hip & trendy) winner — concept, atmosphere and quality on the Esplanade Simone Veil.
Gault&Millau-listed Italian restaurant by Saint-Denis, cooking for three decades.
Gault&Millau-listed Chinese restaurant on the Ourthe quays at Angleur.
Gault&Millau-listed: chef Hyun Frère's creative, refined cooking on the Route du Condroz.

places.ad: Rue de la Casquette 13, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Wine bar on the pedestrian Rue de la Casquette, one of the tourist office's picks for an apéritif and a Culture Trip best bar of Liège.
Outremeuse institution in the heart of Roture — terrace across the square in summer, all-night French-song sing-alongs in winter; the tourist office calls it essential.

places.ad: Quai de la Goffe 37, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Fashionable brunch-and-lunch address on the Goffe quay — simple healthy plates and a big terrace looking over the Meuse.

places.ad: Rue de la Casquette 17, 4000 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Italian café on the pedestrianised Rue de la Casquette, known for its pastrami sandwich and coffee.
The brewers of Légia — the beer named for the river that gave Liège its name — born at Brasse & Vous in Rocourt and now brewing on the Quai sur Meuse.
Two-time Diamond Boulet winner of the Confrérie du Gay Boulet (2005, 2006) — classic boulets in sauce lapin with proper frites, near the Carré.
Small bistro in the Carré on both Moustique's boulets list and sommelier Eric Boschman's nine best Liège restaurants.

places.ad: Boulevard de la Constitution 48, 4020 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Warm, all-homemade Outremeuse brasserie whose boulets won the Confrérie du Gay Boulet's Boulet de Cristal in 2021; also good vegetarian dishes.
Boulets specialist near the Sauvenière — several house sauces and generous frites, simple wines.
Family-run Outremeuse table by Saint-Pholien serving Belgian and Liège classics, boulets included.

places.ad: Rue Porte aux Oies 43, 4020 Liège, Belgium
places.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand (2024) in Outremeuse — chef Tom Foguenne's farm-to-table cooking from local organic producers with a natural-wine list; one of two Liège Bibs announced in 2024.

Liège's former central post office on the Meuse, reopened in Sept 2023 after four years' renovation as Liège's first food market — seven independent counters, a bar pouring beers brewed on site, coworking and the ULiège journalism campus upstairs.

Specialty coffee bar on Rue du Palais serving only East-African coffees with Belgian pastries given an African twist; named among Belgium's ten best specialty cafés in the European Coffee Trip awards.
Small high-ceilinged coffee bar opened 2022 on Rue des Mineurs, styled like a brutalist antique shop by Volga's co-founder; pours Wide Awake (one of Belgium's best roasters) single origins.
